premises.text: Girls want friendship and communication in toys, not low-tech dolls like Baby Alive
premises.evidence_span: we've heard from them friendship, they're friends, and communication

premises.text: Patent-pending mesh networking lets wearables communicate device-to-device without a phone
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots is the first wearable device to communicate from device to device. That means girls don't need a mobile phone

premises.text: Friendship color groups, proximity glow, and customizable secret light/vibration messages are the social product experience
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots can be used to send messages, so girls can send each other secret messages in their own languages

premises.text: Open-source Arduino programming lets girls add custom effects and interactions
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots are completely open source. So girls can code them to do whatever they imagine

premises.text: COPPA compliance enables safe girl-to-girl communication
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots are also COPPA compliant, so the girls can communicate with each other completely safely

premises.text: Sold online in packs with interchangeable charms/bands and licensing partnerships that extend the brand
premises.evidence_span: JewelBots are sold online for $69 for one, $99 for the two-pack, and $139 for the Bestie three-pack

value.text: High-tech friendship wearables that empower girls toward engineering
value.evidence_span: every girl feels empowered to become an engineer
